review_evidence: README describes an interactive Lean/Mathlib textbook designed to be read while working through examples and exercises in the repository.
The hydrated snapshot contains 89 Lean files and direct scan found more than 1,200 proposition declarations spanning sets/functions, structures, groups/rings, topology, analysis, and number theory.
Chapter and solution files contain substantial reusable theorem statements and proofs, for example the groups/rings and Gaussian-integers developments.
summary: Retain Mathematics in Lean as a large checked textbook corpus of examples, exercises, solutions, and mathematical formalizations.

review_evidence: Main chapters (C01-C13) all contain definitions, theorems, examples, #check queries, and sorry-marked exercises — e.g., C02/S01_Calculating.lean has 145 lines of ring calculations and examples
Solution files contain complete proofs — e.g., C02/solutions/Solutions_S02_Proving_Identities...lean proves ring/group lemmas like neg_neg, mul_inv_rev

Nearly-empty solution files (Solutions_S01_Getting_Started.lean, Solutions_S01_Vector_Spaces.lean) still have module structure; others have open/variable/noncomputable commands — e.g., Solutions_S02_Measure_Theory.lean has variable declarations for MeasurableSpace and Measure
MIL/Common.lean contains set_option warningAsError false, an executable command per FILTER-007 exclusion
No file is a pure import-only aggregator; all have declarations, commands, or organizational content
summary: Reviewed all 87 files in the Mathematics in Lean work unit. Every file contains formal mathematical content: main chapters have definitions, theorems, examples, exercises; solutions have proofs or proof skeletons; even minimal files contain executable commands (open, set_option, variable, noncomputable) that place them outside pure-import classification. No file meets the high evidence bar for hard exclusion per FILTER-002/004/007. Per FILTER-021/022, uncertainty mandates retention. The previous review's disposition to retain the full textbook corpus remains correct.

review_evidence: MIL/C02_Basics/S01_Calculating.lean: Contains 145 lines of examples, exercises, #check commands, and proofs using ring, calc, nth_rw tactics over real numbers
MIL/C02_Basics/solutions/Solutions_S01_Calculating.lean: Contains 52 lines of complete proofs for calculating exercises using rw, calc tactics
MIL/C11_Topology/S03_Topological_Spaces.lean: Contains 152 lines of topology examples, theorems (aux), #check commands, and exercises with sorry over topological spaces, filters, compactness
MIL/C11_Topology/solutions/Solutions_S03_Topological_Spaces.lean: Contains 180 lines of complete proofs for topology exercises including Banach-Steinhaus related theorem with filter reasoning

MIL/C12_Differential_Calculus/solutions/Solutions_S02_Differential_Calculus_in_Normed_Spaces.lean: Contains 64 lines with a noncomputable section proving a uniform boundedness principle variant using Baire category theorem in normed spaces
summary: Inspected all 5 changed/added files in the Mathematics in Lean work unit. Every file contains formal mathematical content: main chapter files have definitions, theorems, examples, exercises with `sorry` and executable commands (`variable`, `#check`, `section`, `open`); solution files contain complete proofs or proof skeletons with tactics (`rw`, `calc`, `ring`, `nth_rw`, filter/topology reasoning). No file is a pure import aggregator (all contain executable/formal commands beyond imports). No file's searchable content is exactly represented by another indexed document. Per FILTER-002/004/007/021/022/024, uncertainty mandates retention and no hard exclusion criteria are met.
